entries.speaker: narrator
lines: One throne has fallen. Strange — when its lord died, I felt you grow... heavier. More real.
I have ferried a thousand thousand souls. Yours alone has no name on my ledger.
Why is that, I wonder?

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Two lords cast down, and with each, a memory returns to you. A face. A shore. A name half-spoken.
You were mortal once. That much is plain now.
But no mortal walks all the underworlds. What were you?

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: I remember you now. You died — and you ran. From the scales, from the river, from every judgment laid before you.
So death could not keep you whole. Each afterlife seized a shard of your soul as you fled.
Six shards. Six lords. That is why you are scattered, wanderer.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Four shards reclaimed. You stand almost whole — and I see in your eyes that you remember why you ran.
You were afraid of the weighing. Of what the scales would say you were.
Only two deaths remain to face that fear.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: One shard remains, held by the last lord of the dead.
When you take it, you will hold your whole self again — your name, your deeds, your weight.
Then there is no more running. Only the road, and what waits at its end.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: It is done. Six lords of death lie behind you, and the last shard returns to its place.
You are whole, wanderer. You remember your name — and you no longer fear to say it.
The scales were never your enemy. Only the running was.
Step onto the river one last time. This crossing leads not down, but up — into the light you fled so long ago.
Go. The cycle is broken. You are judged at last, and found... enough.
